findings.what_changed: The published post-fix band (58.69/58.79/59.05/59.27/59.96/60.44/60.59s, 'still straddling 60 on two of seven') does not reproduce at that rate. Before rewriting anything, tested the load hypothesis directly rather than asserting it: 6 runs at ambient load average 2.3-4.9 gave 58.97-59.41s, and one run under artificial CPU load built specifically to test it -- 8 processes pinned at 100% CPU, load average driven to 8.4 on a 14-core machine, concurrent with the suite -- gave 58.96s, the low end of the range rather than the high end. Heavy CPU contention did not slow the suite, because its wall clock is dominated by fixed sleeps and Playwright timeout bounds, not CPU cycles. Combined with the reviewer's 8 runs (59.00-59.87) and the orchestrator's 6 runs at load average 3.19 (58.97-59.22) plus its committed gate run (59.15), ~22 runs across three independent measurers -- idle and deliberately loaded alike -- landed at 58.96-59.87s, none over 60. The two published outliers could not be attributed to load (the one condition tested) or reproduced by anyone at that point, so they were dropped as unsubstantiated and WALL_BUDGET_S reverted 70 -> 60, taking acceptance branch 1. A first commit (073311b) shipped that revert with the full sweep: evals/run.py, fast-wall-clock-budget's boundary rows/expect/env_override, ADR-013 Decision 4 and its header (Ruling/Amends/Route)/Decisions 2-3, ADR-002 Decision 4 and its status header, INDEX.md, .github/workflows/eval.yml's comment, tasks/TODO.md's M12 branch line and M14's headroom note, and README/docs/analysis.md/docs/support-matrix.md, all with a fresh committed baseline run (evals/report/20260821-224446-fast.json, 98/98, 59.35s) replacing the stale pre-fix 60.51s/97-case citation. That commit's own claim -- 'headroom against the max reproducible run (59.87s) is ~0.13s' -- was then checked against itself before declaring the finding closed, per this repo's own recorded pattern of declared limitations getting falsified quickly. It did not hold: 21 further real (non-stubbed) fast runs against the exact committed tree found the honest band is 58.83-60.26s, and the first of those 21 -- ordinary load, no concurrent stress -- measured 60.26s, over the ceiling just reverted to. The next 20 stayed under 60 (58.83-59.81s). Across all evidence gathered for this finding -- the withdrawn 7-run band, both reviewers' 15 runs, and this repair's 43 further runs (22 before the revert, 21 after) -- 3 of 50 total runs landed over 60s, all by 0.26-0.59s, none tied to CPU load by the one direct test against it: a real, low (roughly 2-6% depending how the withdrawn 7 are weighted), unexplained tail, not the ~29% the withdrawn band claimed and not zero either. A second commit corrected the record rather than let the falsified '~0.13s headroom' claim stand: ADR-013 Decision 4, ADR-002 Decision 4, TODO.md, README, docs/analysis.md and docs/support-matrix.md were all edited to state the honest 58.83-60.26s band and the residual risk instead of a false clean margin, and fast-wall-clock-budget's provenance gained a 7th falsification entry recording that the revert's own headroom claim was itself falsified within the same review round. WALL_BUDGET_S stays 60 -- the weight of the evidence (94-98% of runs, honestly counted, clear it) still supports acceptance branch 1 over keeping 70 on an unreproduced load story -- but the ADR now says plainly that a red fast gate at 60.0-60.6s should prompt a re-run before being read as a regression, rather than implying a guaranteed margin that a second round of verification immediately disproved. R16's earlier fix (making the ADR consistently say 70) is not disturbed by reverting to 60 -- checked line by line rather than blind-reverted, since the whole point of that fix was internal consistency, which both round-5 rewrites preserve at the new value.
